evidence.quote: Samples of Ni-based superalloy RR1000 were cold rolled using two different processes (UDCR and 2DCR) in order to investigate the effects of post deformation texture and recrystallization on the development and stability of special R3 n boundaries.

Despite an identical annealing treatment of 1140 /C176 C for 10 min that resulted in a grain size of * 11 lm for all three samples, Fig. 10a, the CR 5 Y–5Z sample was found to contain a denser distribution of R3 boundaries compared to CR 10Y and CR 10Y–10Z where few twin boundaries can be seen per grain.

The length fractions of R9 and R27 boundaries were calculated for the samples in a range of grain sizes, as shown in Fig. 11 and Table 3.
Finally, large rolling reductions prior to annealing resulted in a signiﬁcant decrease in number and fraction of twin boundaries, Fig. 10c, especially for sample CR 20 Y.
When comparing results from both sets of rolled samples, however, sample CR 5 Y–5Z contained the highest overall densities and fractions.
It is also interesting to note that the density and fraction of R3 boundaries in sample CR 10 Y–10Z were higher than that found in the CR 15 Y and CR 20 Y samples.

For each group of UDCR and 2DCR samples, specimens that were subject to the smallest amount of reduction, respectively, CR 5 Y and CR 5 Y–5Z, showed a signiﬁcant improvement of the grain boundary character of the material after annealing when compared to the undeformed and heat treated material, Figs. 9 and 11.

For equivalent average grain sizes, the Goss texture that formed in the 2DCR samples during deformation led to relatively higher densities and fractions of R3 boundaries when compared to the h110i//LD and h111i//RD texture measured in the UDCR samples, as shown in Figs. 7 and 8.

If a critical level of strain energy is stored, recrystallization will occur during annealing and remove all pre-existing R3 boundaries while increasing the population of random and high-angle grain boundaries, Fig. 4.

If a critical level of strain energy is stored, recrystallization will occur during annealing and remove all pre-existing R3 boundaries while increasing the population of random and high-angle grain boundaries, Fig. 4.

With little to no recrystallization occurring in samples CR 5 Y and CR 5 Y–5Z after annealing, they exhibited the lowest ratios indicating that grain boundary interactions occurred during SIBM and led to a highly interconnected grain boundary network with the presence of R9 and R27 boundaries as well as the incorporation of convoluted R3 boundaries in the random grain boundary network, Fig. 10b.
This complex grain boundary structure formed due to twin regeneration as well as the migration of the grain boundary network in a microstructure containing pre-existing twins.
